Reviewed with the incident remediation; update only with source-path review and executed behavior regressions. Relay route registrations remain mounted, but heartbeat, submission, executable delivery, approval and result reporting fail closed. The private unwired resolver is compiled only in tests; production continues to resolve through the custody bridge. One listener configuration, 14 transport configuration and 6 listener boot tests passed. This does not add a listener or a fallback. Source-lifetime review: service admission refuses an expired source; status reports quarantined and expired generations unloaded and preserves revocation precedence. The focused admission, status and source-owned trust collision tests and integrated deadline controls passed. The listener wraps its signer and preclaim session cache with generation checks; source-owned listeners disable resumption. Signer, resumption-race and TLS 1.2/1.3 regressions exercise those boundaries. Testkit files support those regressions and add no production authority. An in-flight key operation or a signature released immediately before withdrawal cannot be revoked, and already-admitted work is not cancelled. Standalone client and server configurations are outside the listener fence. Host source-trust selection requires the generation-bound authoritative source bundle with the requested profile and kind. On the reviewed predecessor, all 16 selector correspondence vectors, the exact two-bundle return control, and the live reconstructed-manager TLS regression passed. The correspondence module is compiled only for tests and adds no production authority. That regression reuses an in-memory store; it is not a process restart or a real Workload API test. Durable source history remains a separate boundary. Peer-domain review: a SPIFFE bundle carries its explicit domain, certificate validation and SVID checks precede peer evidence, and service binding uses exact SPIFFE identity with separate leaf revocation. The configured Host source domain must match the authoritative selected bundle. The peer-domain, live TLS admission, resumption/rotation, forwarded-evidence and wrong-domain controls passed; the correspondence proves only its stated Boolean properties, not Rust refinement. The NATS client opts into a one-use server verifier with TLS resumption disabled; existing host-listener verification remains unchanged. Source-history review: before the final lint changes, the registered history suite passed 76 Linux tests in 16 groups, including SQLite union and cancellation, the cooperative file lease, offline attestation, a real bindings-only Host startup, source supersession, stored-trust quarantine and reconciliation. The lint-corrected source still needs the full suite rerun. The Host-process case does not prove secure-listener or request-guard enforcement. The complete attestation, continuous database identity and cooperative trusted filesystem are assumptions; raw writers, older binaries, backup rollback and physical power-loss durability are not proved. Windows-only startup and initializer refusal tests have not been run on Windows. The proof suite separately pins the executed migration inventory; its hashes do not establish implementation refinement.

Privileged operator migration intentionally handles wrapped vault/private/org keys, server verifiers, API keys and TOTP/recovery material. This is local secret custody, not anonymous export. Source IDs never choose local filenames; archive child paths are opened no-follow under retained roots, regular single-link files and actual file/HTTP byte intake are bounded. SQLite archive row counts are not globally capped by this control. Credential-bearing API requests retain their selected origin; signed file downloads use the API origin or a separately user-authorized storage origin, carry no account bearer and refuse redirects. Live files use random exclusive scratch names. Non-Unix archive file bytes fail closed; see operator compatibility documentation. 2026-10-31: crates/provider-bitwarden/Cargo.toml now pins aes 0.9.2 and cbc 0.2.1 with features alloc and block-padding unchanged (cipher 0.5.2). Encrypt and decrypt still use PKCS7 via encrypt_padded_vec and decrypt_padded_vec; type-2 HMAC is checked before decryption. reqwest, response caps, and origin pinning in that manifest are unchanged. cargo test -p opensesame-provider-bitwarden passed, including response_limits (13), pinned_origin (5), crypto unit tests, and fast crypto vectors. Ignored production-KDF and regenerator tests were not run. bitwarden-server import path tests were not re-run; this diff does not change those sources. 2026-11-07: crates/bitwarden-server/Cargo.toml changes only [dev-dependencies] tokio-tungstenite 0.29.0 -> 0.30.0 (supersedes Dependabot #2514). cargo tree shows no normal-edge path to tungstenite 0.30, so the import implementation, its path confinement, byte bounds and origin pinning link nothing new; upstream 0.30 only rejects malformed Sec-WebSocket-Key on its server side and raises rand/sha1 (already in the lockfile), while the crate's own WebSocket server stays on axum's tungstenite 0.29. cargo test -p opensesame-bitwarden-server --tests passed (lib unit tests incl. import/tests.rs, account_files_tests.rs and file_paths_tests.rs: 49; import 6, import_files 3, import_orgs 3, import_paths 2, import_root_handles 1, import_sign_in 2; device_login 4 and live_sync 4 exercise the bumped client). cargo test -p opensesame-provider-bitwarden --test response_limits --test pinned_origin passed (13, 5). Ignored bw CLI oracle tests were not run. 2026-11-17: reviewed the account import, download destination validation and regressions after requiring exact scheme, host and port for each authorized attachment origin. Additional storage origins are supplied explicitly by the importer, not by the server; rejected attachments are counted as left behind. The provider suite and account_files importer tests passed, including unauthorized and authorized cross-origin cases. The external Bitwarden oracle was not run. 2026-11-17: reviewed live account attachment count and aggregate byte reservations, retained scratch files and bounded re-reads. Failed downloads remain charged; skipped or unreadable files are counted. The 51 server unit tests, import_files, import_paths and import_root_handles integration tests, and CLI bridge tests passed. The limits are per live import; archive row counts remain outside this control.

LOCAL device-owner process custody only. Original session/scope and transport-bound completions retain ownership; cancel, expiry and lock synchronously revoke provisional key/body/VFS custody. Before configured factors and trusted quorum complete, a revocable private IAM handle permits only bounded policy/directory/credential reads and genuine WebAuthn assertion-counter advancement, with no ordinary VFS, key export or consumable IAM sign-in evidence. Activation and leases publish once under their original owner; metadata, preferences and device-key reconciliation retain operation checks. Bound regressions use genuine sealed stores, real contact assertions and controlled completion boundaries. Copied vault artifacts with primary unlock material can be decrypted outside this local gate: this is neither offline cryptographic quorum nor global lifecycle enforcement. Source fingerprints require deliberate source-path review and executed relevant regressions after every change; they do not prove crash atomicity or cancel already accepted physical writes. 2026-11-10: classification-cross.ts gains one shared rule, for lib/tailscale-key-prefix. That module holds only the provider's key-prefix strings and a function that joins them; the native Tailscale connector and tailnet devices both import it, and until now it matched no rule, so the classification test failed on main. The rule grants no capability and changes no existing rule, including the private-IAM and WebAuthn helper rules this row binds. Passed: every test under apps/pages/src/lib/capabilities (204 tests in 24 files), classification.test.ts among them.
